scope: Independent source-package validation of the user-selected streaming progress and PowerShell launcher change.

permitted: Synthetic local executables and repositories under this validation run
Read-only source snapshots and byte-bound authoring intake
Local Python and PowerShell subprocesses without network access
prohibited: Live Claude or other model invocation
Credentials, network access, installation, operational skill updates, or production data
fixture_boundary.oracle: Expected results are derived from the user-approved behavior and legacy public contracts; fixtures do not import product parsing or policy code.

denominators.first_party_executable_source: All Python files under scripts/ and evals/ in the exact delivered package. The PowerShell launcher is separately measured when a supported PowerShell coverage tool is already installed; otherwise all of its required behavior is covered by native black-box cases and PowerShell line coverage is reported NOT_RUN, never inferred.
exclusions: Markdown, YAML, and JSON declarative resources
Python standard library and PowerShell runtime

requirements.requirement: The run CLI accepts an optional --show-progress flag; omission retains the existing quiet JSON transport behavior.
requirements.level: compiled CLI equivalent / local Python CLI

requirements.requirement: Progress mode invokes Claude with --output-format stream-json and --verbose while preserving the existing restricted read-only execution profile.
Progress is emitted only to stderr and exposes bounded safe metadata; prompts, assistant response bodies, tool payloads, and credentials are not emitted.
The helper emits exactly one final machine-readable JSON result on stdout.
Raw child stdout and stderr, the exact terminal envelope, and a validated response are retained with digests when applicable.
Malformed JSONL, a missing terminal result, duplicate terminal results, and malformed terminal result envelopes are rejected without manufacturing a response.
One monotonic deadline covers stream reads, pipe EOF, process exit, stderr collection, and cleanup.
Timeout and cancellation perform bounded cleanup and record whether the launched process stopped.
Streaming attempts use a versioned receipt that binds transport, command, inputs, artifacts, status, and terminal envelope.
Existing advisor-execution-v1 receipts remain valid, immutable, and usable as prior history for one permitted follow-up.
The two-attempt limit, immutable request, attempt reasons, per-attempt budget reservation, and child-only auth policy remain enforced.
A failed or budget-terminated terminal envelope retains finite reported cost without treating it as a valid response or as authoritative billing proof.
The thin advisor.ps1 launcher runs under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7, forwards request, run-dir, briefing, reason, and show-progress exactly, and propagates the Python exit code.
The PowerShell launcher contains no duplicate auth, budget, evidence, validation, command construction, or retry policy.
Instructions, runtime documentation, deterministic JSONL cases, schemas, and artifact manifest describe and bind the delivered behavior without claiming native Claude or framework acceptance.
